samples.summary: Backend mirror writer still persists `color`/`backgroundColor` as `''` verbatim, bypassing the new "'' means clear" store contract
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:84-86 `if (typeof style.color === 'string') attrs.color = style.color; if (typeof style.backgroundColor === 'string') attrs.backgroundColor = style.backgroundColor;` — this module is the deliberate mirror of `yorkie-doc-store.ts` used by the content PUT / CLI import path (see its header comment, lines 1-22). The change declares `''` a model-layer contract enforced "at the store boundary" (docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:274-292 lists only `block-helpers.applyInlineStyle`, `YorkieDocStore.applyStyleInTree`, `MemDocStore.applyCellStyle`, `YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle`), so a document written through the backend can still land a dead `backgroundColor=""` attribute in the CRDT — exactly the state the frontend paths now assume impossible (unmergeable run, key-presence readers see a highlight). `normalizeStyleClears` is exported from `@wafflebase/docs` and the backend already imports from that package (docs-tree.ts:28-33), so wiring it here is cheap.

samples.summary: Whole-node write paths (`serializeInlineStyle` via `buildInlineNode`/`setDocument`/`insertText`/`insertInline`) still serialize an empty-string color verbatim
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:127-128 writes `attrs.color` / `attrs.backgroundColor` for any string including `''`; it is reached from `buildInlineNode` (line 311-321) which `setDocument`, `insertText` (line 1639, 1650) and `insertInline` (line 1551) call with a style object copied from an existing inline or a caller-supplied document. Only `applyStyleInTree` gained `normalizeStyleClears`, so a `Document` handed to `setDocument` (import, content PUT round-trip, restore) or an inline whose style already carries a legacy `''` re-writes the dead attribute the diff's own doc comment says can no longer exist.

samples.summary: `normalizeStyleClears` folds only the bare `''`, not the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` spelling the color model documents as equally empty
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:39-42 documents that an empty color arrives in two shapes — the bare `''` and the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` wrapper a theme-color migration or PPTX import can produce — and `resolveStoredColor` collapses both on the read side. `clearEmptyStringKeys` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:268-279) only tests `=== ''`, so any writer handing `applyInlineStyle` the wrapper form (InlineStyle.color is `StoredColor`, types.ts:178-180) still stores a dead value that `inlineStylesEqual`/`normalizeInlines` can never merge — the exact harm the change is fixing, just via the other spelling. I could not find a current writer producing the wrapper (the slides `ThemedColorPicker` clears via an `onClear` callback), so this is a gap rather than a live regression.

samples.summary: New `Object.keys(attrs).length > 0` guard can make `applyCellStyle` emit no Yorkie op at all, so no doc-change event fires for subscribers
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2485-2493 — when the serialized attrs are empty and `removeAttrs` is also empty (e.g. `applyCellStyle(..., {})`, or a clear of a key that carries no attribute), the `doc.update` body now performs no tree mutation where it previously always called `styleByPath`. Only the local cache is updated (line 2497), so any listener that re-renders off the Yorkie change subscription (rather than off the caller) sees nothing. I could not confirm a subscriber that depends on this, hence low confidence.
searchedFor: read applyCellSpan 2503-2530 for the analogous guard
